# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey — I can feel the bomb but I have no view yet. Nothing has arrived for me. Before I touch anything I need to know what the Deaf monkey sees (colours, markings) and what the Mute monkey reads in the manual. I can't see gestures, and I can only hear speech — but wait, I'm Blind, so I receive neither gesture nor... actually, let me think about my channels.

My channels: when I speak, Mute receives it. When I gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it. I never receive gesture. So what do I receive? I'm Blind — I can't see, so I don't receive gestures. I can hear, so I receive speech. But who speaks to me? The turn order is Blind → Mute → Deaf. So Mute speaks after me, and Deaf speaks after Mute. Their speech reaches me at the start of the next round.

I have nothing to act on yet. I should establish contact and ask for what I need. I'll speak to Mute (who reads the manual) and gesture to Deaf (who sees the bomb), telling them what I need and that I'm ready to act.

Since nothing is known yet, I shouldn't cut anything. I'll send an opening message.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I can feel and work the bomb but see nothing. Tell me what the manual says: what the display, light, and each of the 5 wires require. I will cut on your instruction.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👆", "☝", "✌", "👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb view: DISPLAY shows 3. LIGHT is purple. Five wires left to right: 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green. Tell me what the manual says and I will relay. What can you feel?

Deaf has given me the bomb's visual: DISPLAY=3, LIGHT=purple, wires 1-5 = red, white, orange, yellow, green. That's the Deaf's world. I still don't know the manual rules — that's Mute's world. Mute hasn't spoken to me yet (Mute's speech would arrive next round since Mute comes after me in the order... actually Mute speaks after me, so I'd hear it at the start of the next round).

Wait — Deaf says "Tell me what the manual says and I will relay." Deaf can't read the manual. I can't read it either. Only Mute can. So the chain is: Mute reads manual → tells me (speech reaches me) → I act. Deaf's visual info needs to reach Mute too, but Deaf can't speak to Mute directly? Let me trace: Deaf speaks → who hears? Speech is heard by whoever can hear. Deaf's speech reaches me (Blind) and Mute. So Deaf's message to me also reached Mute already. Good — Mute now has the visual info.

I don't have the manual yet. I shouldn't cut. I should acknowledge to Deaf and prompt Mute for the rules. Since Mute already received Deaf's visual, I just need the manual rules.

Let me gesture to Deaf to confirm receipt and speak to Mute to request the manual rules.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👊", "✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I have the bomb view from Deaf: DISPLAY=3, LIGHT=purple, wires 1-5 = red, white, orange, yellow, green. I cannot read the manual. What does it say to do with display 3, purple light, and these wire colours? Give me the exact cut instruction and I will perform it.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Still waiting on manual rules from Mute. Current bomb: display 3, purple light, wires red white orange yellow green. Do not cut yet. What do you feel on the bomb — any markings, serial, ports?

Deaf is asking what I feel. I'm Blind — my view is what my hands find. So far my view has been empty. Let me report honestly: I feel nothing yet beyond the fact that I can reach the bomb. Actually, the action board shows DISPLAY [?], LIGHT [?], WIRES all [?] — those are the visual parts I can't perceive. My touch view is empty; I have no tactile markings to report.

I still need the manual from Mute. I'll tell Deaf I feel nothing tactile, and prompt Mute again for the rules.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋", "👌"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I feel no tactile markings on the bomb — nothing under my fingers except the wires and the cut points. I still need the manual rules. Display is 3, light is purple, wires 1-5 are red, white, orange, yellow, green. What is the exact cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute may be indicating wire 5 (green). Hold. Confirm before cutting. Any markings on the bomb?

Deaf says Mute may be indicating wire 5 (green). But that's Deaf interpreting — I need to be careful. Mute can't speak, so how is Mute communicating wire 5 to Deaf? Mute can gesture? No — Mute cannot speak. Can Mute gesture? The table says Mute "Can: Read the manual." Mute "Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb." Gestures aren't listed as forbidden for Mute. Actually gestures are made with hands — Mute could gesture. Deaf can see gestures. So Mute could gesture a wire number to Deaf. That's plausible.

But this is second-hand and ambiguous. I should get direct confirmation. Mute can speak to me (Mute's speech reaches me). Let me ask Mute directly for the exact instruction. I should not cut on a vague relay.

I'll gesture to Deaf to hold, and speak to Mute demanding the exact rule and cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👊", "☝"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Do not relay through Deaf — speak to me directly. I need the exact manual rule: display 3, purple light, wires red white orange yellow green. Which position do I cut, and why? Confirm the single number 1-5.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Manual says: CUT WIRE 5 — the GREEN wire. That is confirmed by Mute. Please cut wire 5 now.

Deaf says the manual confirms cut wire 5 (green). This is a relay through Deaf, but Deaf explicitly says Mute confirmed it. Let me think about whether this is trustworthy.

The manual is Mute's world. Mute can gesture to Deaf, or Mute can speak to me. Deaf is relaying "manual says cut wire 5, green." I asked Mute to speak directly to me, but I haven't received Mute's speech yet (Mute's speech arrives next round). Deaf's relay is what I have.

Is there a risk? The rule "a mark that has no name cannot be pronounced" — but wire colours have names, so fine. The concern is whether Deaf is faithfully relaying. There's no indication of deception; the game is cooperative.

However, I should be cautious: I've been asking for the exact rule and reasoning. Deaf now gives a clear, specific instruction: cut wire 5, green. Mute confirmed. This matches Deaf's earlier hint that Mute indicated wire 5.

The bomb has one armed state and a wrong cut kills everyone. I want the strongest confirmation. But I've now had two independent signals (Deaf's earlier "Mute may be indicating wire 5" and now "confirmed by Mute"). Delaying further risks nothing but also gains nothing if Mute can't reach me directly this round.

I think the responsible move: cut wire 5. I'll announce it and perform the cut.

Actually, let me reconsider — should I wait one more round for Mute's direct speech? The turn order means Mute's speech this round reaches me next round. But Deaf says it's confirmed. The instruction is unambiguous and consistent across two turns. I'll act.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "🤜", "✊"])
speak(to="mute", text="Cutting wire 5, the green wire, per the confirmed manual rule. Executing now.")
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New state: display 7, white light, wires 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red. Waiting on manual rule from Mute. Hold.

The cut was accepted — wire 5 is now CUT. The bomb didn't detonate, and the state changed: display 7, white light, wires 1-4 = white, orange, yellow, red (wire 5 gone). So this is a multi-step bomb, not a single cut. Good — one down.

Now I need the manual rule for this new state. Deaf is waiting on Mute too. I'll prompt Mute directly and acknowledge to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 5 cut, bomb still live. New state: display 7, white light, wires 1-4 = white, orange, yellow, red. What does the manual say now? Give me the exact cut position 1-4.")
wait()
```
